subject: Re: Canary safety provisions & conditional autorevert authorization
body:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@ledgerone.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Diaz <elena.diaz@ledgerone.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Canary rollout and SLA question — automatic rollback/pinning

Hi Marissa,

Quick question as we finalize the pilot schedule: LedgerOne's procurement requires written confirmation of what happens to our SLA guarantees during the canary/A-B windows. Specifically: if latency or error-rate regressions are observed in the canary cohort, will Redwood automatically revert traffic (autorevert) or pin to the previous model version until telemetry stabilizes? We need this behavior spelled out for our security/compliance review and the SOW.

If autorevert is an opt-in, what guardrails do you require (metrics, minimum sample size, time window)? Also: will a revert trigger an incident that affects uptime calculations under the SLA, or is that treated as a mitigation action outside credit calculations?

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Ops, LedgerOne
samir.khan@ledgerone.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@ledgerone.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Sep 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary rollout and SLA question — automatic rollback/pinning

Hi Samir — thanks for raising this. Short answer: we can offer a conditional autorevert + version-pin provision for the pilot, but we need to document the exact trigger logic and carve out how that interacts with SLA uptime/latency credits.

High-level proposal (attached matrix and playbook):
- Conditional autorevert: automatic rollback to the previously pinned model variant when a pre-defined latency or error threshold is breached for the canary cohort for a sustained window.
- Pin behavior: when pinned, traffic is routed back to the pinned version for the affected route/region until manual verification or an automatic recovery window completes.
- SLA impact: changes made as mitigation (autorevert/pin) will not count as downtime for the purposes of SLA credit calculations provided the action follows the approved playbook and is executed within the documented timelines. If the mitigation itself causes customer-visible regression outside the playbook, normal SLA rules apply.

Guardrails we propose for LedgerOne pilot (we can iterate):
1) Metric triggers: median token-latency increase > 30% for canary cohort AND 99th percentile latency > baseline + 300ms OR error-rate (status >=500 / timeout) > 1.5x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes.
2) Minimum sample size: at least 1,200 requests in the canary window to avoid noisy signals.
3) Sustained window: conditions must hold for at least 10 minutes and be observed on two consecutive metric buckets.
4) Automated notification: on trigger, an automated revert will begin and PagerDuty + email alerts will be sent to LedgerOne and Redwood on-call.
5) Rollback timeline: traffic rollback should complete within the same routing epoch (target < 90s) and KV-cache warmup is accounted for in the playbook.

Attachments: SLA_conditional_rollback_matrix.xlsx (matrix of triggers / exemptions) and Canary_Playbook_v2.pdf (step-by-step ops flows).

Next steps: if this aligns, Laura and I will prepare a one-paragraph contract amendment and Ops runbook excerpt to include in the SOW. Please confirm preferred thresholds or tell us which metric weights you want tightened.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Sep 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary rollout and SLA question — automatic rollback/pinning

Marissa — thanks for the draft. From a commercial and legal perspective I support treating documented mitigation actions as outside of downtime calculations, provided we: (a) strictly follow the published playbook, (b) keep an audit trail (timestamps, trigger buckets, decision logs), and (c) limit autorevert to the affected route/region.

I propose two small changes before we finalize the amendment:
- Reduce the median-latency delta trigger to >25% (LedgerOne is latency-sensitive).
- Add a manual approval bypass window: for severe incidents (error-rate > 3x baseline), the on-call may elect direct manual rollback immediately; that event should still be logged for audit but will be eligible for normal SLA credit if it results from platform failure.

If engineering signs off, I'll instruct Legal to add the amendment text and the playbook excerpt to the SOW.

Laura Bennett
Head of Global Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary rollout and SLA question — automatic rollback/pinning

Thanks — quick technical notes from infra:
- The proposed trigger thresholds are implementable. We can tighten median-latency to >25% as Laura requested, and we will add a smoothing window to avoid single-bucket noise.
- Autorevert mechanics: our routing layer supports per-route version pinning and immediate traffic shift back to the previous variant with an expected completion time of 60–120s depending on model size and KV-cache behavior.
- Auditability: we will emit an immutable event to the customer's audit log (s3 log + console entry) and attach the trigger snapshot. We'll also capture pre/post latency histograms and the canary sample ids for reconciliation.
- Caveats: if the pinned variant requires a different quantization profile, there may be a short tail in successful-response rate during warmup; we recommend a 5-minute controlled observation after rollback before marking the incident closed for the SLO ledger.

If everyone agrees, I'll queue the playbook snippets into the Canary_Playbook_v2.pdf and add the event schema for Legal/Compliance.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Product Manager, Platform | Redwood Inference
